name: Sursock Museum
watch: Fondation Engie, a gas utility, is an energy sponsor.
why_flagged: Fondation Engie, a gas utility, is an energy sponsor.
records_note: Sursock posts its 2025 annual report, named supporter lists for 2024 to 2026, and its board of trustees, but no financial statements.

name: The MAC
funding: £3.0M income (FY2025). Arts Council NI £1.1M, Belfast City Council £120k, Freelands Foundation £126k, Art Fund, Henry Moore Foundation, Dormant Accounts; sponsors include Clever Fulton Rankin.
watch: Operates under Northern Ireland Charity Commission regulatory standards.
records_note: The NI register holds annual reports 2023 to 2024 and accounts to 2025; the supporters page shows tiered logos without names, and trustees are listed.

name: Crystal Bridges
funding: Walton family endowments; the Walmart Foundation gave $7M in 2023 to keep admission free through 2028. FY2024 expenses were $96.1M against revenue of $131.2M, with $37.2M in contributions.
watch: Walmart Foundation is a current funder. Walmart's anti-union policy draws documented criticism; the museum's funding sources are a point of debate. No protest turned up.
records_note: Annual reports 2017 to 2020 as videos, Form 990s 2014 to 2023 on ProPublica, a dated 2025-26 supporters list, and the board listed.

name: Gropius Bau
funding: €12M. Berliner Festspiele, Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media.

name: Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW)
funding: €18M. Federal Government Commissioner for Culture and the Media (BKM), Auswärtiges Amt.

name: KW Institute for Contemporary Art
funding: Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, KW Friends, Berlin LOTTO-Foundation (bought the buildings), Schering Stiftung, Casa Camper. Julia Stoschek Collection is a programme partner.
watch: Core-funded by the Berlin Senate. BMW Group sponsors select commissions under an arms-length cultural agreement; KW adheres to the Berlin Senate Code of Conduct for public cultural bodies with transparent reporting.
why_flagged: Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, KW Friends, Berlin LOTTO-Foundation (bought the buildings), Schering Stiftung, Casa Camper. Julia Stoschek Collection is a programme partner.
records_note: The institute names its 27-member board and its main funders in text, but publishes no annual reports or accounts.

name: Staatliche Museen zu Berlin
funding: Federal government pays 71% of the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation's €275M operating budget, Berlin 14%, other Länder 7%. Sparkassen-Finanzgruppe is main sponsor, renewed in 2017.
watch: Governed under the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation (SPK). Major public funding; corporate partnerships are regulated by federal public procurement and anti-corruption guidelines, though historic colonial provenance remains under active restitution review.
records_note: Parent SPK posts annual reports 2016 to 2025 and budget figures; SMB names only supporter groups and patrons undated, and no council members.

name: Kunstmuseum Bern
funding: Canton Bern and the Burgergemeinde's museum foundation fund it. UBS is main sponsor; Mobiliar and UNIQA sponsor exhibitions; eight funding foundations include Hansjörg Wyss's Stiftung GegenwART.
watch: UBS paid a $100M US Federal Reserve fine in 2004 for dollar trading with Iran and other sanctioned countries.
records_note: Annual reports 2016 to 2025 with full accounts, an undated partner page naming UBS, sponsors and foundations, and a listed foundation board.

name: De La Warr Pavilion
funding: £3.9M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £518k and Rother District Council £477k core; Esmée Fairbairn, Art Fund, Levelling Up Fund, National Lottery Heritage Fund.
records_note: Stakeholder and impact reports run 2018-19 to 2025; accounts 2021 to 2025 are on the Charity Commission register; funders and trustees are named.

name: Eastside Projects
funding: Arts Council England National Portfolio, Birmingham City University (partner since 2008), and trusts including the Paul Hamlyn, Esmée Fairbairn, Jerwood and Henry Moore foundations.
watch: Its undated supporters list credits Genting Casino alongside past funders such as the Future Jobs Fund. No current gambling funding found.
records_note: No annual reports; Companies House holds micro-company accounts to March 2025; the supporters list is cumulative and undated, and no board is listed.

name: Ikon Gallery
funding: Arts Council England supports it with National Lottery funding. Current corporate patrons: Deutsche Bank, Elonex, Howells, Kier and Transport for West Midlands.
watch: New York regulators fined Deutsche Bank $150M in July 2020 for ignoring red flags on Jeffrey Epstein's accounts. No protest at Ikon turned up.
records_note: Annual reviews 2023 and 2024 are online; accounts are on the Charity Commission register; corporate patrons are named, undated; trustees are listed.

name: Cranbrook Art Museum
funding: Exhibition credits name MillerKnoll, Gilbert Family Foundation, DeRoy Testamentary Foundation and Clannad Foundation. The Gilberts pledged $30M in 2021 to Cranbrook Academy of Art, which also backs museum projects.
watch: National Historic Landmark in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Cranbrook Educational Community posts Form 990s 2020 to 2025 and its trustees, and the museum lists no donors.
